newsitem.title: USA: Interactive Flight gets $30 mln contract.
newsitem.headline: Interactive Flight gets $30 mln contract.

text.p: Interactive Flight Technologies Inc said Monday that Swissair Schweizerische Luftverkehr AG agreed to purchase its in-flight entertainment network in a contract valued at more than $30 million.
Under terms of a memorandum of understanding, Swissair expects to purchase the system for installation in the first and business class sections of up to 18 aircraft, the company said.
Swissair will pay cash for the systems as they are installed, and Interactive Flight and Swissair will negotiate the split of revenues generated from gaming, the company said in a statement.

As previously reported on March 18, Interactive Flight had exercised its right to begin discussions with Swissair regarding renegotiation of its contract to install the entertainment network on Swissair planes. This follows a decision by Interactive Flight to concentrate its efforts on marketing the system to airlines willing to commit their own resources.

The company also said today that PrivatAir has signed a non-binding letter of intent to purchase from Interactive Flight at least one in-flight entertainment network for installation on its Boeing 757 aircraft. The network is scheduled to be installed about six months following the execution of a purchase agreement, the company said.
Interactive Flight provides in-flight, interactive digital entertainment, including casino-style gaming, video-on-demand, video games and interactive shopping.
Shares of Interactive Flight were trading up 3/16 to 5-3/4.
